post.summary:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access + refresh pair.

`@Public()` by necessity: a client arrives here precisely because its
access token has expired, so it has no bearer credential to present. The
refresh token in the body IS the credential. A legitimate client
refreshes once per access-token lifetime, so 10/min per IP is ample.

post.summary:
Re-issues a pending invitation on a fresh code, which it returns; the old
code stops working.

Guarded by `create WorkspaceInvitation`, not `delete`: re-issuing is the
same authority as inviting — same person, same role, same workspace — and
gating it behind `delete` would leave a manager able to raise an
invitation they could not repair when the code was lost.

200, not 201: nothing new comes into existence. The invitation is the same
row, carrying a rotated secret.

post.summary:
`@AuthenticatedOnly()`, not `@Public()`.

The code is bound to the invited account, so the caller must be signed in
as that account; accepting never creates one (only an administrator does,
`POST /users`).

No permission is required because there is none that could apply: authority
inside the workspace is precisely what this call grants.

delete.summary:
Gives back an upload the caller will not attach — a replaced pick, an
attach that was refused. It still counts toward the limit of unattached
uploads until the cleanup job deletes it, within minutes. Releasing it
again is safe. Someone else's file, an unknown id, or one already deleted
is 404; the caller's own file that is attached (or still being processed)
is 409 `FILE_NOT_RELEASABLE`: remove it from what shows it instead.

parameters.name: assignableIn
parameters.description:
Narrows the list to roles the caller may actually assign inside this
workspace — workspace-scoped, and at or below their own rank there.

This exists because an assignment UI that lists every role invites a
request that is guaranteed to 403, and worse, tells a curious admin exactly
which roles sit above them. The rank ceiling is enforced on write no matter
what, so this is ergonomics rather than a control; but a picker that only
offers reachable options is the difference between a boundary users
understand and one they probe.

password.description: At least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes in UTF-8.

deviceTokens.description:
The `deviceToken`s earlier sign-ins on this device were given, for any
accounts (a shared laptop holds several). One for the account signing in
marks a device it has used before, which a stranger's failed guesses at
the account cannot lock out (`SignInDeviceTokenService`).

contentType.description: The type the server identified from the file's content.

url.description:
A signed URL that reads the file until `urlExpiresAt`. Minted only after
the caller was authorized to read the resource it belongs to. It is a
bearer credential — do not log or share it; read the resource again for a
fresh one.

profileImage.description: The profile picture, with a short-lived URL; null when none is set.

isPasswordChangeRequired.description:
The password was chosen by an administrator (a new account, or a reset)
and must be replaced before anything else: every other route answers
PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED until `PATCH /users/me/password` succeeds.

deviceToken.description:
Keep it with this device and send it in `deviceTokens` at the next
sign-in: a device the account has signed in from is not locked out by
someone else's failed guesses. Not a credential on its own — the password
is still checked — and replaced by every sign-in.

refreshToken.description:
The refresh token issued by `POST /auth/login` or a previous
`POST /auth/refresh`.

Bounded on both sides so a malformed or hostile body is rejected by the
validation pipe before it reaches a database lookup. The generated token is
32 random bytes in base64url — 43 characters — so the window is generous
enough to survive a future change of token length without being an open
door for megabyte-sized payloads.

The refresh token held by this device, so the session chain is closed and
not just the access token.

Optional, because logout must still succeed for a client that has already
discarded it (or never stored one). Omitting it revokes only the access
token this request arrived on — which leaves the refresh token able to mint
a new one, so clients SHOULD send it.

platformRoles.description: Names of the platform roles held by the caller. Empty for most accounts — platform roles are STAFF roles, and self-service capability comes from the intrinsic authenticated-user grants rather than from a role. An empty array is normal, not an error state.

workspaceMemberships.description: Every workspace membership the caller holds, in ANY status. Only `active` ones contribute to `rules`; the rest are context so a client can show a pending invitation or a suspended membership rather than silently omitting it. Never infer authority from this list — read `rules`.

fileId.description:
The picture, as the `id` returned by `POST /files` with
`purpose: profile_image`. It must be your own upload and not yet attached:
someone else's file, one uploaded for another purpose, or one the cleanup
job already removed is 404; a used, expired or released one is 409
`FILE_NOT_ATTACHABLE`. Either way, upload it again.
Sending the id of the current picture changes nothing. To remove the
picture, use `DELETE /users/me/profile-image`.

ownerEmail.description:
The email of the existing account that will own the workspace. It must be
an ordinary account: a platform account never belongs to a workspace
(`PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_CANNOT_JOIN_WORKSPACE`). An unknown email is
`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. The creator does not become a member.

email.description:
The email of the existing account that becomes the workspace's sole owner.
It must be an ordinary account (`PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_CANNOT_JOIN_WORKSPACE`).
Every current owner becomes `workspace_admin`.

password.description: At least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes in UTF-8 (a character such as ñ takes 2, an emoji 4), with a letter and a digit.

roleId.description:
The workspace role the new account joins with. Bounded like adding a
member: at or below the creator's own rank, and only `workspace_staff`
without role-assignment authority (`ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE`).

identifier.description:
The email or username of the account to invite. Pakita has no public
sign-up, so the person must already have an account (an administrator
creates it).
